questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place that had a lot to explore, so I had a lot of options during my entire stay.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A great, great experience that I would recommend to everyone! I loved it a lot and got so many fantastic experiences. The only downside was practical stuff like how hard it was to find a place to live and how expensive the rent was.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. UoE sends mails about everything (especially all the events that take place in the first week).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was extremely hard. Would not recommend :'))) I got my room 5 days before I arrived after I called 5 million times. I had to pay 10.000 DKK each month for a small room in a shared dorm. I tried for idk 4 months before arrival to find a room on spareroom and Facebook, but I couldn't find anything. Some of the other KU students did find accommodation through those, so it is possible! Try it and start looking before you think you should. If you do want student accommodation or can't find another option, keep calling the accommodation office multiple times a day until they give you a room. That's how every exchange person I got to know got theirs. Good luck :')))

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The quality of the housing I lived in did not live up to the price. But it was a good location, so it was fine!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy enough, but took some time. They had an online slot-system where you had to sign up for appointments to get your registration and library card (which was necessary to get acces to the library and exams). The wait for the library cards was over and hour in the first days, so go later if possible.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call and email the offices.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted, and got a lot of help from the office. They were really nice and helpful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the emails sent to your university mail and call the office if you need help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked my courses. Take 1st year courses if you just want easy courses, and take 3rd-4th year courses if you want some really interesting (but a little harder) ones. I had a mix and enjoyed that. The only downside on the academic front was that the course was really short (9-10 weeks long), so you did not have that long to understand the course material as on KU - but it's nice if you want to have a lot of time to explore :)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My 1st year course was veeeery basic (we learnt how to make references and write academic texts, which you probs know if you're going away on 5th semester of your bachelor or later). My 4th year course was quite hard and high level, but really interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same with some lectures and some smaller discussion classes (that were much smaller in size with around 8 people in each class)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Mapping Health and Illness Across Societies (SHSS08001) and The Functional Organisation of Visual Cortex - A Cognitive Neuroscience Approach (PSYL10164)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're interested in neuropsychology, I would really recommend "The Functional Organisation of Visual Cortex - A Cognitive Neuroscience Approach". It was really interesting and high-paced. Loved the classes.

questions.answer: Above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UoE has soooo many social clubs (I think it was around 270), so you'll find something you want to join! I can recommend the hillwalking society that has cheap weekend trips to hills throughout Scotland (and England). It was an amazing way to experience both a lot of Scotland, but also hillwalking with experienced "guides". Also a great way to meet a lot of local students and other exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds you could possibly imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hillwalking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and put some new friends in it. Go on weekend trips around the country and rent some AirBnB's or sleep in tents.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies and speak to people in your lecture halls/classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pubs, hills, the outdoor life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Say yes to as many things as you can fit in to your stay with as many nice people as you can find (but also save some time for recharging)
2. Go on trips around the country - it's amazing
2. Start looking for a place to live really early (boring, but nice to know)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature experiences I got and the amazing people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to seek out things to do and people to spend time with in the first part of my stay. Took a looot of energy, but it was also rewarding. Also missing the people at home, but it's fortunately an easy destination to visit ;)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
